Musa Manzani - surviving brain surgery whilst playing guitar

By: Julian Sun | Production

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
We tell the remarkable story of Jazz Musician Musa Manzini - who survived brain surgery whilst playing guitar

Unique Selling Point:
Musa Manzini is a celebrated jazz musician and a maestro with the bass guitar. But he really shocked the world when he played his guitar while undergoing brain surgery. Now he’s back home and on the road to a remarkable recovery.

Summary:
Musa Manzini is a celebrated jazz musician who is known for his work on tv series like Generations & Backstage. Having returned from working abroad in Indonesia in February last year to take up a teaching position at the University of KZN, he noticed a numbness in his left hand. This turned out to be a result of a recurring tumour in the brain.

To cure him, a rare awake craniotomy was performed on him in December 2018 to remove a recurring brain tumour at Inkosi Albert Luthuli Central Hospital in Durban. I

Musa was awake during the six-hour operation to avoid paralysis or loss of functions in the part of the brain that controls voluntary movement.
Manzini said he was made to play a guitar during the procedure.


The craniotomy was performed by a team of specialist resident neurosurgeons led by Dr Basil Enicker and Dr Rohen Harrichandparsad.

On Carte Blanche we interview Musa about his remarkable story.

We also chat to the 2 neurosurgeons from Albert Luthuli Hospital who performed the craniotomy on Musa, Dr Basil Eniker & Dr Rohen Harrichandparsad

We chart the events that led up to the surgery, the operation itself as well as Musa's recovery

Press Release:


A Man, a Guitar and a Brain Tumour

Musa Manzini is a celebrated jazz musician and a maestro with the guitar. But he shocked the country when he was filmed, playing his guitar while undergoing brain surgery. Keeping a patient awake during a craniotomy is a well-known practice, but in South Africa, playing a guitar as surgeons work to remove a tumour, has been hailed as ground-breaking. Now Manzini is back home and on the way to a full recovery.

Producer: Julian Sun
Presenter: Macfarlane Moleli
Research: Siniketiwe Hlanze

Script:


INTRO VOICE OVER:

Imagine you were born with a great musical ability

And you were able to harness that talent to forge a successful career

How would you feel if that livelihood and perhaps even your life was threatened?

That’s what confronted a renowned jazz musician again last year when he discovered he had a brain tumour.

What’s more he would need to be awake and play guitar during the surgery to remove it

This is Musa Manzini’s remarkable story








V/O: Musa Manzini was born in Inanda Kwa Zulu Natal in 1971. He enjoyed a typical upbringing until his seminal teenage years where he fell in love with music for the first time

Comments from Musa on growing up and discovering his love of music

V/O: Musa’s older sister Thembi remembers her brother’s passion for music with great fondness.

Comment from Thembi about Musa’s musical passion.

V/O: Musa studied a musical degree at University before embarking on a successful career becoming a renowned jazz bassist.

Over the years, he has played with some South Africa’s best musicians, toured the world and released several of his own acclaimed albums.

Comment from Musa about the highlights of his career.

V/O: By the mid-2000’s Musa was on top of the world, but then the rug was pulled out from under him

Comments from Musa & Themba about the first and second occurrences of Musa’s tumours

V/O: Following the removal of the second tumour, Musa made the decision to leave South Africa and settle Indonesia, hoping that the change of lifestyle would prevent the tumour from recurring.


V/O: Having spent 4 years living abroad, Musa felt the call of home. It was whilst working as a music teacher at UKZN that he noticed a numbness in his left hand



Musa on the tumour returning

V/O: And worse news was to follow when Musa’s medical aid refused to pay for another operation. It meant that his only alternative was to approach a government hospital for help

Musa & Thembi on the fear of going to a public hospital

V/O: Their fears about having to turn to a government hospital for help were allayed when they met the excellent neurosurgical team of Dr Basil Eniker & Dr Rohen Harrichanparsad at Inkosi Albert Luthuli Central Hospital in Durban

Comments from Doctors about meeting Musa and explaining what was wrong with him

Musa comments about having to be awake and play guitar during the operation.

V/O: Operating on such a sensitive part of the brain is a delicate procedure, where the slightest error could affect Musa’s ability to play music. This is why they chose to perform an awake craniotomy

Comments from Musa & Thembi about their fears

Comments from Musa & doctors about Musa being awake during the operation.

V/O: Following the 6-hour procedure, the doctors declared the operation a success.

V/O: Remarkably less than a week after major brain surgery, he was allowed to go home to his sister’s house in Richard’s Bay where he has spent the last month recovering.

Comments from Musa about feeling coming back to his hand, about headaches, about getting stronger and fat

Comments from Thembi about cooking for him, about how quicker his recovery has been compared with previous operations

Comments from Doctors about his recovery and how happy they are with his progress, about the tumour recurring

V/O: The last few months have certainly been eventful for Musa Manzini. Not only has he survived brain surgery but he was also able to provide a soundtrack to one of the most remarkable days of his life.

Now well on the road to recovery, what does he take away from what has been an extraordinary journey?



OUTRO: Whether the tumour returns remains to be seen, but for now Musa remains positive, taking one day at a time and living by the maxim that it’s the simple things in life that are the most extraordinary



Promo Scripts

10”: Playing the bass is something celebrated jazz musician Musa Manzini can do easily – but playing a guitar while undergoing brain surgery, was one of the toughest challenges of his life.


15” Promo 1: Celebrated Jazz musician Musa Manzini not only survived brain surgery but did it whilst wide awake and playing guitar.
Musa comment:

15” Promo 2:

He’s a celebrated jazz musician and a maestro on the bass.  But he shocked the world when he played guitar while undergoing brain surgery.

Musa Comment

30” Promo: Imagine you were blessed with great musical ability that you were able to harness to forge a successful career

But then a brain turmour causes you to lose feeling in your hands

With your livelihood threatened and your life in danger your only alternative is brain surgery

But there’s a catch, you have to be awake during the procedure

Comment from Musa

This is Musa Manzini’s remarkable story.
